newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Russian minister says wage arrears will be paid.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister says wage arrears will be paid.

text.p: Russian Economy Minister Yakov Urinson said on Thursday that wage arrears to public sector workers would be paid mainly by improving tax collection.

Urinson told a news conference at the second Central and Eastern European Economic Summit the government would also collect debts owed to the cental authorities by companies such as gas monopoly Gazprom and power company Unified Energy System.
"The debt will be paid above all by, as the last two and a half months has shown, an improvement in tax collection," Urinson, who is also a deputy prime minister, said.

First Deputy Prime Minister Borias Nemtsov said on Wednesday Russia would pay off 5.4 trillion roubles ($935.1 million) in back wages to the military by September and 25 trillion roubles in other public sector arrears by the end of the year.
Some economists had noted that the Russian government had not given full details of how it would raise the money.
President Boris Yeltsin had originally wanted all arrears paid off by October 1 but Nemtsov said the Kremlin leader had since signed a new decree ordering the back wages paid by the end of the year.
"The promise made by President Yeltsin will be fulfilled just as we fulfilled the promise to pay off the debts to pensioners in the first half-year," Urinson said.
Minister without portfolio Yevgeny Yasin said prices had risen 8.5 percent this year and the money supply by 24 percent.
He said that together these factors were causing some tension in the economy but described this as "a normal healthy process".
Yasin said the first stage of Russian economic reform had been completed and the achievements would make the next stage easier.
"Although I don't think I should be over-optimistic here. I cannot make any rosey statements about the near future," he said.
